summary: Both sides are centered, resolution-independent radial figures that cycle the full hue wheel at nearly the same rate, but the original is a blazing white core throwing thin curved streamers across a mostly-black field while the port is a filled, ~4x brighter spiral vortex with a DARK core that only creeps around instead of erupting.
observations: Neither side has any controls: probe reports '(no settable controls)' for both, so the control surface matches and there is nothing to dial.

Both sides render cleanly on the default 16x16 grid rig for the whole 240 s survey - no compile or runtime errors, no decay, no freeze (zeroMotionFrames = 1 on both, i.e. only the first captured frame). Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both).

Structure, original: a single very bright near-white core at grid center with fast radial falloff, and a handful of thin, smoothly curved streamers reaching to the edge over an otherwise black field. Radial mean brightness (dump-radial, 16x16, t=1/3/6/9 s) runs r1 ~150-213, r2 ~45-82, then only ~7-34 at r3-r6.

Structure, port: a bright core PLUS a dark annulus at r=2-3 PLUS a broad bright ring/spiral filling r=4-6. Same dump: r1 ~180-207, r2 ~50-55, then r4-r6 back up to ~57-177. The mid-field the original leaves black is where the port puts most of its light.

Fill/duty, same dump: counting pixels above 20/255 on each radius ring, the original lights 2-9 of 16-36 per ring (sparse filaments, azimuthal CV 1.3-2.9), the port lights 23-36 of 28-36 (near-complete rings, CV 0.34-0.92). The port has no thin rays at all.

Brightness, both sides untouched: original meanBrightness avg 22 (baseline 6 s / 20 fps), 20 (survey 60 s / 5 fps), 21 (survey-240); port 83 / 66 / 59. The port is roughly 3-4x too bright, and that is fill, not gain - its core is about as bright as the original's.
Motion magnitude: original motion avg 5.9 / 16.4 / 25 at 20 / 5 / 2 fps; port 1.4 / 5.1 / 15. motionLit tells the same story (baseline 9.9 vs 1.5), so it is not a sparseness artefact.

Motion character (baseline and grid48 filmstrips, consecutive 20 fps frames): the original's streamers whip and sweep around the core, growing, curling and dissolving visibly every 0.05 s frame; the port's spiral is near-identical across the whole 0.55 s strip, with only the white arm creeping - roughly a quarter to a third of a turn over 5.5 s in the survey-240 filmstrip (120.0-125.5 s).

Colour: both walk the entire hue wheel continuously (magenta -> red -> orange -> yellow -> green -> cyan -> blue -> magenta). Hue-vector autocorrelation of the meanR/G/B series gives a period of 13.0 s (2 fps) / 13.2 s (5 fps) for the original and 12.0 s at both rates for the port - a close match, port about 9% faster, and both fps-invariant so neither side is frame-rate-coupled.

Both sides are resolution-independent: re-rendered at --grid 48x48 each draws the SAME logical picture as at 16x16, just finer (original: smooth curved filaments off a star; port: a smooth spiral arm around a dark hub). That axis matches.

Both sides are seed-independent: seed 7 and seed 1234 produce byte-identical meanBrightness series to each other on both sides, so neither pattern is stochastic and the divergence is not an RNG artefact.
No mode/regime rotation on either side: over 240 s at 2 fps each side keeps one continuous look, and a parked late window (--skip 120, 20 fps) shows exactly the same two structures as t=0.
feedback: The topology is inverted in the mid-field. The original's brightness falls off monotonically from a hot core (r1 ~200 -> r2 ~60 -> r3-r6 ~10-30 on a 16x16 grid); the port dips to a dark annulus at r=2-3 and then peaks again at r=4-6 (~100-180). Remove the bright outer ring/halo and let brightness decay outward from the core instead.

The field should be mostly black. The original lights only 2-9 pixels of each radius ring (15-30%); the port lights 60-100% of them and posts 3-4x the mean brightness (66-83 vs 20-22). The target look is a few discrete filaments over darkness, not a filled disc.

Draw RAYS, not a spiral. At 48x48 the original is several distinct curved streamers that leave the core in different directions and reach the edge; the port is one continuous spiral arm wrapped around a hub. Feature count and radial reach are the things to fix - the smooth curved-filament rendering itself already looks right.

The port is far too placid. The original's arms visibly re-form frame to frame at 20 fps (motion 5.9, motionLit 9.9); the port holds essentially the same image for half a second (motion 1.4, motionLit 1.5) and only slowly rotates. It needs eruption/turbulence - streamers that appear, extend and dissolve on a ~0.5-2 s timescale - rather than rigid-body rotation of a fixed shape.

The original's overall brightness fluctuates strongly and quickly (meanBrightness 7-48 over the survey, autocorrelation decaying by lag 2-3 frames at 5 fps, with some moments nearly dark); the port's is smooth and slowly varying (43-96). Whatever drives the eruptions should also modulate total output episodically.
Keep the hue behaviour - it is already close. Both walk the full hue wheel; just slow the port slightly, from a ~12.0 s cycle to the original's ~13.1 s.
Do NOT add controls: the original exposes none, and the port correctly exposes none.
